newsitem.title: USA: Paxson to sell radio holdings to Clear Channel.
newsitem.headline: Paxson to sell radio holdings to Clear Channel.

text.p: Paxson Communications Corp., the largest owner of television stations in the United States, said Monday it had agreed to sell its radio holdings to Clear Channel Communications Corp. for $693 million cash.
Paxson said it would use the proceeds to complete previously announced TV station acquisitions.

In a press statement, Paxson said the tax-advantaged transaction includes its 46 radio stations, six radio news and sports networks, and two minor league sports teams, as well as its billboard division. The sale is subject to Federal Communications Commission approval, anti-trust clearance, and definitive agreements, the company said.

"Paxson Communications will use sale proceeds to complete the announced TV station acquisitions," said Paxson Chief Executive Lowell Paxson. "We will now focus and capitalize on our high growth television holdings."
Paxson said it had been holding talks with major broadcast networks, Hollywood movie studios, cable programmers and syndicators "to forge the foundation of a new broadcast television network."
Paxson said last week that it had agreed to acquire the operations of U.S. Travel Channel, a 24-hour cable network, from Landmark Communications Inc in a $75 million transaction.
